Documentary photograph aesthetic, unretouched, fine film grain.

A psychologist's desk in daylight, seen from slightly above. A woman's hands enter from the right edge, typing on a pale keyboard; a thick manual lies open beside it, its pages softly out of focus, print reduced to an even grey texture, a finger of the left hand holding the place. The monitor sits beyond the top edge of the frame. The moment of typing the same line again. Focused, weary, unposed.

FG: the open manual, slightly below centre. MG: the hands and the keyboard, occupying the right third. BG: the monitor stand and a plain wall, softly defocused.

Light: cool morning daylight from a window on the right, soft; the left side of the desk falls into gentle shade.

Composition: rule of thirds. The keyboard and the hands fill the right third; the lower left quadrant is calm bare desk, left clear for copy added later.

Angle: high three-quarter, just above desk height, with comfortable margin around the subject on all sides.

Focus: hard focus on the fingertip holding the page. Set to 50mm, medium depth of field so the background stays readable during a slow dolly in.

Tone: Low Saturation Gray palette, muted grey-green and warm beige. Natural skin texture with visible pores, matte skin with no shine, believable proportions and natural hands.

The subject reads clearly against the background in tone and value.

Overall vibe: three hours of retyping.

The desk surface is bare and unmarked, the manual pages an even grey texture free of legible print, every surface clean and free of lettering.
